authoritative_sources.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and driving: A Canadian Thoracic Society and Canadian Sleep Society position paper
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Thoracic Society and Canadian Sleep Society
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CTS guideline library lists this Canadian position paper as under review; it remains the listed Canadian source and explicitly defers licensing decisions to provincial authorities.

supported_recommendations.statement: When counselling a driver with obstructive sleep apnea, explain that licensing authorities make restriction decisions under provincial rules; clinical fitness assessment considers symptoms and treatment response rather than OSA severity alone.

source_citations.locator: Recommendations for assessing fitness to drive in noncommercial drivers, key messages 1–3

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Commercial-vehicle fitness assessment should be more stringent; provincial requirements govern implementation.

source_citations.locator: Recommendations for assessing fitness to drive in noncommercial drivers

evidence_boundaries.statement: Do not use OSA severity in isolation to determine fitness to drive.

evidence_notes: Limited to counselling and Canadian fitness-to-drive context.

authoritative_sources.title: Silicosis
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Fact sheet lists revision 2024-03-25 and page modification 2025-08-28; current CCOHS page checked on retrieval.

supported_recommendations.statement: In a patient with suspected occupational fibrotic lung disease, obtain a focused exposure history for respirable crystalline silica and relevant work tasks; silicosis results from inhalation of free crystalline silica and risk varies with dust characteristics and exposure duration.

source_citations.locator: What causes silicosis; Who is at risk of developing silicosis
What causes silicosis; Who is at risk

evidence_boundaries.statement: Silicosis risk assessment depends on exposure, not on smoking history alone.

evidence_notes: Canadian occupational-health authority used because no current CTS pneumoconiosis diagnostic guideline was listed.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: CCOHS is the current Canadian authority directly addressing silica exposure and occupational risk recognition; CTS guideline library did not list a current pneumoconiosis diagnostic guideline.

authoritative_sources.title: Canadian Thoracic Society COPD Action Plan (Educator's copy)
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: CTS continues to publish this action plan in its current COPD resources; the CTS 2023 pharmacotherapy guideline explicitly excludes acute-exacerbation treatment.

supported_recommendations.statement: A severe acute COPD exacerbation complicated by acute respiratory failure is a medical emergency requiring urgent escalation; short-acting bronchodilators treat dyspnea/wheeze and systemic prednisone is included for moderate-to-severe flare-ups in the CTS action plan.

source_citations.locator: Pharmacological Treatment; Severe AECOPD complicated by acute respiratory failure

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Antibiotic selection in a COPD flare-up is individualized by clinical risk factors; it is not automatic for every exacerbation.

source_citations.locator: Antibiotic Treatment Recommendations for Acute COPD Exacerbations

evidence_boundaries.statement: The action plan distinguishes severe exacerbations with acute respiratory failure from outpatient flare-up care.

source_citations.locator: Severe AECOPD complicated by acute respiratory failure

evidence_notes: Emergency scope restricted to initial recognition, escalation, and action-plan stabilization.

authoritative_sources.title: Immunization of persons with chronic diseases: Canadian Immunization Guide
authoritative_sources.guideline_version: Current online Canadian Immunization Guide chapter
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Official current Canadian Immunization Guide chapter; page lists April 10, 2026 update.

guideline_versions: Current online Canadian Immunization Guide chapter

supported_recommendations.statement: COPD prevention should include smoking cessation and vaccination; for chronic lung disease, annual influenza vaccination is recommended and pneumococcal vaccination follows current Canadian age- and risk-based guidance.

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: In current severe asthma or active wheezing, live attenuated influenza vaccine is contraindicated and non-live influenza vaccine should be used.

evidence_boundaries.statement: Pneumococcal vaccine selection is age- and risk-sensitive, not a single schedule for every adult with COPD.

evidence_notes: High-freshness vaccine specifics retained only as supported by the current PHAC guide.

authoritative_sources.title: Technical guideline to asbestos exposure management programs
authoritative_sources.issuing_organization: Employment and Social Development Canada, Labour Program
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Current federal technical guideline; regulatory specifics apply to federal workplaces and illustrate the prevention hierarchy, not provincial legal requirements.

supported_recommendations.statement: Prevent occupational fibrotic lung disease by controlling respirable dust exposure through hazard assessment and the hierarchy of controls, prioritizing elimination/substitution and engineering controls; respiratory protection is an adjunct selected according to monitoring and the work context.

source_citations.locator: Hazard investigation, risk assessment, control measures and respiratory protection

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: The asbestos technical guideline’s regulatory details apply to federal workplaces; provincial and territorial workplaces follow their applicable occupational-health legislation.

source_citations.locator: Introduction; applicability of Canada Labour Code occupational health and safety regulations

evidence_boundaries.statement: Medical surveillance may identify early disease but does not replace exposure control.

source_citations.locator: What should be included in a medical surveillance program

evidence_notes: Canadian occupational-health authorities supersede a general specialty-source target for this workplace prevention requirement.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: CCOHS is the current Canadian authority directly addressing silica exposure control; no current CTS pneumoconiosis prevention guideline was listed.

authoritative_sources.title: Sleep Apnea
authoritative_sources.currentness_notes: Official PHAC page remains available; its lifestyle measures are stable background prevention guidance and do not replace specialist diagnosis or treatment guidance.

supported_recommendations.statement: For mild obstructive sleep apnea and risk reduction, support weight management and exercise, smoking cessation, avoidance of alcohol and sedating medications before sleep, regular sleep timing, and side sleeping where appropriate; confirm diagnosis and individualize treatment rather than presenting lifestyle change as universal definitive therapy.

source_citations.locator: Lifestyle changes; Lose weight; Get moving; Stop smoking; Avoid alcohol and sleeping pills; Sleep on your side

important_contraindications_or_exception.statement: Alcohol and certain sleeping or pain medicines can worsen airway obstruction and prolong apneic pauses; do not frame them as sleep-apnea treatment.

evidence_boundaries.statement: Lifestyle measures may resolve symptoms in some mild sleep apnea but do not obviate diagnostic confirmation and individualized treatment.

evidence_notes: Canadian authoritative alternative used because CTS’s listed adult sleep-apnea documents are under review or in update, whereas this packet is limited to stable prevention guidance.

source_family_target_assessments.rationale: PHAC directly supports the bounded prevention requirement; CTS lists the adult sleep-apnea guideline as update in progress and the driving paper as under review.
